tier_reason: Neither half of this repo is a runnable application. apps/web is a TypeScript library (tsconfig sets noEmit, package.json has no start/dev/serve script and no server, framework or HTML entry point) and services/pricing is a Python package (no __main__, no ASGI/WSGI app, no HTTP framework in its dependencies — its dependency list is empty). There is nothing to start and no URL to screenshot, so renders is unreachable; both suites build and run, so build_and_test is the ceiling.

commands.install: (cd apps/web && npm ci && npm install --no-save --no-package-lock "@vitest/coverage-v8@$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(require("./node_modules/vitest/package.json").version)')" @microsoft/eslint-formatter-sarif) && python3 -m venv "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bsf-venv/pricing" && "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bsf-venv/pricing/bin/python" -m pip install -e "./services/pricing[dev]" pytest-cov
commands.coverage: rm -rf /tmp/bsf-coverage && mkdir -p /tmp/bsf-coverage && (cd apps/web && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --coverage.enabled --coverage.provider=v8 --coverage.all --coverage.include="src/**" --coverage.reporter=lcovonly --coverage.reportsDirectory=/tmp/bsf-coverage/web) && (cd services/pricing && COVERAGE_FILE=/tmp/bsf-coverage/.coverage "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bsf-venv/pricing/bin/pytest" -q --cov=pricing --cov-report=lcov:/tmp/bsf-coverage/pricing.lcov) && sed "s|^SF:|SF:apps/web/|" /tmp/bsf-coverage/web/lcov.info > /tmp/bsf-coverage/lcov.info && sed "s|^SF:|SF:services/pricing/|" /tmp/bsf-coverage/pricing.lcov >> /tmp/bsf-coverage/lcov.info

static_checks.name: eslint
static_checks.why: The static gate runs its own eslint only when node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js sits at the repository root. In this monorepo eslint is installed in apps/web/node_modules, so the built-in never fires and the TypeScript half of the repo was checked by nothing. This runs the repo's own eslint 9 with its own eslint.config.mjs, from apps/web so the flat config applies, and emits SARIF through @microsoft/eslint-formatter-sarif (installed by commands.install, not added to package.json). Its artifactLocation URIs are absolute file:// URIs, so the gate relativises them to apps/web/src/... and counts per rule per file.

static_checks.name: ruff
static_checks.why: The static gate runs its own ruff only when pyproject.toml or ruff.toml sits at the repository root. Here pyproject.toml is in services/pricing, so the built-in never fires and the Python half was checked by nothing either. ruff emits SARIF natively (0.17.6 is installed). It is run from the repository root over the services/pricing path so that its absolute file:// URIs relativise to services/pricing/pricing/..., and ruff's own hierarchical config discovery still picks up the E, F, B, SIM, RET, ARG selection from services/pricing/pyproject.toml — confirmed by an ARG001 finding on a scratch file.

dropped.what: actions/setup-python@v5 with python-version 3.12 and actions/setup-node@v4 with node-version 22
dropped.why: Those pin the toolchain for CI's runner. The sandbox uses whatever python3 and node the runner already has; pyproject requires-python is >=3.11 and the web app pins no engines, so both are satisfied without a setup action. Recording it because it is the one place the repo states a version, and a future failure on an older interpreter should be traced back to here.

dropped.what: Two separate jobs (web, pricing) with path filters, so a PR touching only apps/web does not run the Python suite
dropped.why: The split is a CI scheduling optimisation, not something the app needs installed. The sandbox is one environment for both apps, and the factory's gates decide which tools to run for a given change. Running both suites in the sandbox is the safe direction: the cost is seconds, and the contract in CONTRACT.md is exactly the thing a single-app run would miss.

dropped.what: pip install -e '.[dev]' run against the runner's interpreter directly
dropped.why: CI gets away with it because actions/setup-python provides an interpreter that is not marked externally-managed. The trial job runs no setup-python, so the system python3 on a current Ubuntu runner would reject a bare pip install under PEP 668. The sandbox creates a virtualenv instead and installs into that; it is the same install, just somewhere pip is allowed to write.

dropped.what: tsc as a static_checks entry, alongside eslint and ruff
dropped.why: The type check is already the build (tsc --noEmit is the whole of apps/web's build step), so a type error fails the build and the change never reaches the ratchet. tsc has no SARIF output and the factory has no built-in TypeScript checker, so making it a static_check would mean writing a diagnostic-to-SARIF converter with nowhere in this repo to keep it. Left as a build failure rather than a counted, baselined finding — which means a pre-existing type error could not be baselined and tolerated, but there are none.

exercised: apps/web: TypeScript type checking of src/ and test/ under strict and noUncheckedIndexedAccess (tsc --noEmit)

apps/web: eslint 9 flat config over the whole package (js recommended + typescript-eslint recommended), twice — once in the build, where a finding fails it, and once as the `eslint` static check, which writes SARIF so the gate can count findings per rule per file and ratchet them
apps/web: the vitest suite, 9 tests, including the five rounding rows from CONTRACT.md and the TypeError/RangeError guards
services/pricing: ruff check with the E, F, B, SIM, RET, ARG rule selection from pyproject, twice — once in the build and once as the `ruff` static check, which writes SARIF for the same reason
services/pricing: the pytest suite, 10 tests, including the same five rounding rows and the half-up-not-half-to-even case

Line coverage for both languages in one lcov report: @vitest/coverage-v8 over apps/web/src and pytest-cov over services/pricing/pricing, each run through the same test invocation as commands.test, path-prefixed to the repository root and concatenated. Measured here: 3 files, 100% of lines (apps/web/src/basket.ts 5/5, services/pricing/pricing/__init__.py 2/2, services/pricing/pricing/basket.py 19/19), so diff coverage is measurable for a change to either language.

The cross-language contract itself: both implementations are checked against the one table in CONTRACT.md in a single test command, so changing one language's rounding without the other fails here. Verified by truncating instead of rounding half up in services/pricing/pricing/basket.py — 4 Python tests failed, 0 TypeScript tests failed — then reverting.
Editable installation of the pricing package, so a change to pricing/ is picked up by the tests without reinstalling

not_exercised.what: Anything rendering in a browser, and any end-to-end check of a running process
not_exercised.why: There is no application to start. apps/web compiles with noEmit and exports three functions; it has no HTML, no DOM code, no bundler and no dev server. services/pricing exposes a module API and has no HTTP framework or entry point. There is no URL for the trial to open and nothing for a screenshot to show.

not_exercised.what: The web app actually calling the pricing service over a wire
not_exercised.why: README.md describes the relationship as 'the web app asks the service what a basket costs', but no code implements it — there is no HTTP client in apps/web and no server in services/pricing. The sandbox verifies that the two implementations agree on the same table of values, which is what the repo really enforces; it cannot verify a request/response path that does not exist yet. A change that introduces one needs an amendment to add the service and its URL.

not_exercised.what: Coverage of anything outside apps/web/src and services/pricing/pricing
not_exercised.why: The vitest half is scoped with --coverage.include="src/**" and the pytest half with --cov=pricing, which is every source file either package has today. A new TypeScript source directory outside apps/web/src, or a second Python package beside pricing/, would be invisible to the report — not measured as zero, but absent, which the coverage gate treats as 'nothing measurable' rather than a failure. Widening either scope is a one-flag amendment.

not_exercised.what: Per-rule counting and baselining of TypeScript compiler diagnostics
not_exercised.why: tsc --noEmit runs in the build, so a type error fails the change; but it produces no SARIF and the factory has no built-in TypeScript checker, so its diagnostics are not counted per rule per file by the static gate and cannot be baselined. In practice this only matters if a pre-existing type error ever needed tolerating; there are none today.

not_exercised.what: The coverage and SARIF tooling itself is installed at install time rather than declared by the repo
not_exercised.why: @vitest/coverage-v8, @microsoft/eslint-formatter-sarif and pytest-cov are none of them in apps/web/package.json or services/pricing/pyproject.toml, and setup may not change the repo on an amendment. commands.install adds them with `npm install --no-save --no-package-lock` and a plain `pip install` into the sandbox virtualenv, so the working tree stays clean (verified: git status unchanged after a full install) — but it means the versions are resolved fresh from the registries on every run rather than pinned by package-lock.json. The vitest provider is pinned to the installed vitest version at install time, read out of node_modules, so it cannot drift from the runner it instruments.

not_exercised.what: Any persistent state — database, cache, queue, object store, outbound email or any third-party API
not_exercised.why: The repo has none. Both halves are pure functions over integer cents, there is no network or filesystem access in either, no environment variable is read anywhere in apps/ or services/, and there is no Dockerfile, compose file or devcontainer. That is why env, services, stubs and egress are all empty rather than unfilled: the sandbox gives the app nothing because the app asks for nothing.

Grepped apps/ and services/ for process.env, os.environ, getenv, dotenv and config reads, and searched the tree for a Dockerfile, a compose file or a devcontainer.
episode.observed: No match for any configuration read, and no container or devcontainer file exists. Two self-contained libraries with no dependencies beyond their own dev tools: apps/web depends on eslint, typescript, typescript-eslint and vitest; services/pricing declares an empty runtime dependency list and pytest plus ruff for dev. Nothing to configure, nothing to connect to, nothing to start.

episode.observed: All of them pass: 9 vitest tests, 10 pytest tests, no type errors, no lint findings. Chose a virtualenv over CI's bare pip install because the trial job runs no actions/setup-python, so its python3 is the runner's system interpreter and PEP 668 would reject installing into it.
episode.changed: Put the virtualenv under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bsf-venv/pricing rather than inside the checkout. .gitignore covers node_modules, __pycache__, *.egg-info, .pytest_cache and .ruff_cache but has no entry for a virtualenv, so a venv in the tree would be untracked and a role running `git add -A` could commit several thousand files. TMPDIR is one of the six variables the closed environment carries through, and install always runs before build and test, so the path is stable where it is used.

episode.tried: Ran the three candidate command strings verbatim through bash -c from the repository root with env -i, carrying only the PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG and CI that the sandbox's closed environment passes, to check that nothing depends on an inherited variable.
episode.observed: build and test both passed under env -i. install failed there with 'Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement setuptools>=68' — this agent sandbox reaches package registries through a proxy whose configuration env -i had stripped, not a defect in the command; it succeeds with the normal environment, and the trial runner has direct registry access, which ci.yml already demonstrates for the same install. Amendment for the coverage-and-checkers report. Read the runner out of .factory/bin/runner.tgz before changing anything, to find out what the gates actually require: schema/sandbox.json for the shape of commands.coverage, coverage_report and static_checks; runStaticTools, runSarifCheck, countSarif, sarifPath, readCoverage and fromLcov for how the results are read; and .github/workflows/factory-gates.yml for where each gate runs.
episode.observed: Two things decided the design. First, runStaticTools only runs its built-in eslint when node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js is at the repository root, and its built-in ruff only when pyproject.toml or ruff.toml is at the root; this monorepo has eslint under apps/web and pyproject under services/pricing, so neither built-in has ever fired and the static gate has been checking nothing — exactly what the report describes. Second, fromLcov passes each SF: path through rel(root, …), which leaves a relative path untouched, so a report written from inside apps/web would name files the gate cannot match against the changed-file list. The tests gate runs `build && coverage` and the coverage gate reads the report from disk in the same job, so the report only has to survive between two steps of one job.
episode.changed: Settled on one merged lcov report rather than two (the schema allows a single coverage_report), on absolute /tmp paths for the report and both SARIF files so nothing untracked lands in the working tree, and on two static_checks — eslint via @microsoft/eslint-formatter-sarif and ruff via its native --output-format sarif.

episode.tried: Built the pieces one at a time and checked the output of each. ruff check --output-format sarif over `services/pricing` from the repository root, with a scratch file planted in services/pricing/pricing/ to force a finding. eslint with the SARIF formatter from apps/web, with a scratch file in apps/web/src/ holding an unused var, an `any` and a `let` that should be `const`. @vitest/coverage-v8 with --coverage.reporter=lcovonly, and pytest-cov with --cov-report=lcov, each from its own package directory.
episode.observed: ruff reported ARG001 on the scratch file — so the E,F,B,SIM,RET,ARG selection in services/pricing/pyproject.toml is still discovered when ruff is invoked from the root — and wrote an absolute file:// URI, which relativises to services/pricing/pricing/… . eslint reported prefer-const, @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars and @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any, also with absolute URIs; on a clean tree it still writes a valid 846-byte SARIF with zero results, which is what keeps the check from being dropped. Both coverage runs wrote package-relative SF: paths (src/basket.ts, pricing/basket.py), which rel() would have left wrong. Deleted both scratch files and confirmed git status was unchanged.
episode.changed: Added a sed prefix per half — SF:apps/web/ and SF:services/pricing/ — and concatenated the two lcov files into one. Kept each coverage run inside its own package directory so it is the same invocation as commands.test plus flags, rather than a differently-rooted run that might discover different tests.

episode.tried: Wiped apps/web/node_modules and the virtualenv and ran the whole amended manifest from a clean checkout: install, build, test, coverage, then both static checks with the environment stripped to env -i PATH HOME TMPDIR LANG CI, which is what closedEnv passes. episode.observed: install took 14s and left the working tree clean — npm install --no-save --no-package-lock adds @vitest/coverage-v8 and @microsoft/eslint-formatter-sarif without touching package.json or package-lock.json, and the formatter's own eslint 8 dependency stays nested under it, leaving eslint 9.39.5 at the top level. build, test (9 + 10 tests) and coverage all pass; the merged report holds 3 files at 100% of lines. Both SARIF checks produced valid, parseable SARIF under the stripped environment. The runner read both of them and reported them as checkers it could run.
episode.changed: Pinned @vitest/coverage-v8 to the vitest version read out of node_modules at install time, instead of hard-coding 5.1.1, so a dependabot bump of vitest cannot leave the provider on a mismatched major.
